author: reek
body: Both rings hold sixteen descriptors and until this test nothing in the tree drove either past its end: e1000-bringup injects one frame and sends one, dhcp-acquire-e1000 exchanges a handful. So the two places that decide a wrap -- the int-mod in e1000-recycle-rx and the one in e1000-send-at -- had no arm that could tell a correct answer from an absent one. Forty of each against sixteen is two full turns and part of a third.

author: reek
body: The byte total is here rather than a count alone because the count is satisfied by forty frames of anything. e1000-recycle-rx clears the status and length words and deliberately does NOT rewrite the descriptor's buffer address; the model re-reads that address on every placement, so an address damaged on the way round the ring moves this total and nothing else would notice.

author: reek
body: Two and a half turns of a sixteen-entry ring.

author: reek
body: The fuel is the ring size times the frame count, which is far above any honest run and still terminates a driver that reports a frame forever.
